samples.text: The harbour clock had run four minutes fast for as long as anyone could remember. Sailors set their watches by it anyway, because a shared mistake is easier to correct than a private one. On foggy mornings the bell carried farther than the lighthouse, and the ferry waited for its second stroke before casting off.
